committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects all institutions of higher education participating in federal student aid programs, the Department of Education, and students attending those institutions.
dimensions.evidence: institutions of higher education participating in federal student aid programs

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative and compliance duties such as website link placements, physical and digital postings, annual reports, audits, studies, and monthly congressional briefings.
dimensions.evidence: The bill requires an IHE to post a link on its website on how to file a Title VI complaint with OCR.

dimensions.assessment: The source authorizes a public awareness campaign (potentially via contract with a nonprofit) and requires ongoing federal agency briefings, audits, and studies, but specifies no exact dollar amounts.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary may carry out this subsection directly or through a contract with a nonprofit organization that specializes in public awareness communications.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to add institutional requirements, places restrictions on the Office for Civil Rights regarding complaint dismissals, and mandates audits, studies, and congressional briefings.
dimensions.evidence: Section 487(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1094(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent compliance requirements for colleges and universities, alongside a specific one-year requirement for monthly congressional briefings.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act and ending 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act

missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for the cost of the public awareness campaign, audits, and studies.
Exact number of institutions or students that will be affected.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates new reporting, auditing, briefing, and public awareness requirements for institutions of higher education participating in federal student aid programs and the Department of Education.
